# Research log

Dated, append-only notes on what was learned and what changed. Numbers are rendered from
`results/**/metrics.json`.

---

## 2026-09-14: Phase 0, feasibility

### Which design the measurements support

Measured on this laptop, the VRAM-to-PCIe bandwidth ratio is
**4.9×**, not the 20–40× the brief
assumed. Pinned H2D reaches 26.52 GB/s
over a Gen5 x8 link. The brief's claim that fetching offloaded KV is an "arithmetic
impossibility" is therefore wrong as stated. Its conclusion survives on a different
comparison. Fetching a layer's non-resident KV costs
11.5×–13.3×
the time of the best GPU attention kernel over the same tokens
(16,384–262,144
tokens per layer). Compute and H2D overlap almost fully, but only
7.5%–8.6%
of a layer's tokens can be fetched within that window. That figure is a lower bound, since MLP time was
not measured. **Design (b) plus query-aware block selection with selective prefetch is
supported. Dense fetch (a) is not.** Exact CPU partial attention (c) costs
154.15 ms per token at 65,536
non-resident tokens, and it beats fetching only when the CPU tier's layout forces a host
gather or per-block transfers. It stays as a small-set exactness experiment, not a main
path. Arithmetic: `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` §3.

### Measurement incidents (kept because they would have become findings)

1. **Kernel-selection trap.** This Windows torch build has no FlashAttention. Default SDPA
   dispatch with GQA silently uses the math kernel, which is
   33.1× slower than cuDNN
   attention at 65,536 tokens. The math kernel scans KV more slowly than the PCIe link
   transfers it (`SYSTEM_INFO.md` §2 and §3). Timed that way, GPU attention would have looked
   slower than fetching, and design (a) would have looked viable. Fix: every backend is timed and checked against math.
2. **DVFS artifact.** A GPU timing that followed the CPU section in the first smoke test ran
   several times slower than the same operation on a warm GPU (smoke-test output not
   retained, so no number is quoted), because the laptop GPU had
   dropped to its minimum clock. Fix: spin up before every GPU section, and log clock and
   link generation throughout.
3. **Unreproduced low PCIe result.** The very first smoke test reported a pinned H2D figure
   far below every later run (2 quick and 3 full). Its cause is unknown. The output was not
   retained, so no number is quoted. Response: independent process-level runs with
   between-run ranges reported.
4. **Contaminated run discarded.** The first full run overlapped web requests made for the
   related-work survey during its overlap and CPU sections. It was deleted before analysis,
   and all three reported runs ran on an idle machine from a clean tree.

### Other things learned

- `asyncEngineCount` = 1, confirmed by timing: H2D and D2H serialize completely. CPU copies of KV must be written once, never written back.
- Host RAM is a single DIMM (single-channel). Single-thread memcpy runs at 7.78 GB/s, slower than the PCIe link, so host-side gathers are a real cost.
- A 64-token per-layer block (128 KiB) reaches only 43% of PCIe bandwidth as one transfer.
- `expandable_segments` is not supported on this platform.
- Llama-3.2-1B's full 64K bf16 KV fits in free VRAM, so the study's GPU budget is imposed, not forced. The 3B model does not fit in bf16 even at modest context.
